 Order

Petitioners file these petitions for quashing of the FIR No.72/2021 under Section 406/420/468/471/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Chitranjan Park against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.

2. The facts of the case are on 17.11.2018, the complainants/ respondents No.2 & 3 booked through the petitioner No.1 company and were allotted Unit No.R8 G 07, in the Commercial Complex named M3M, 65th Avenue, Sector 65, Gurugram, Haryana (hereinafter referred as the Unit) and subsequently they entered into Buyers Agreement dated 17.11.2018.

Both the respondents No.2 & 3 have paid a sum of Rs.93,70,932/- towards purchase of the unit to petitioner No.1 company and for the balance amount the respondents No.2 & 3 opted for the finance from ICICI Bank / respondents No.4.

A tripartite agreement was executed between the complainants, ICICI Bank and the petitioner No.1 company, whereunder the petitioner No.1 was obliged to make the payment of EMI/
Installments till the possession was handed over to complainants i.e. till March, 2022.

In between some disputes arose qua the non-payment of EMI by petitioner No.1 company to ICICI Bank on behalf of the complainants, hence complaint was lodged by the complainants, which led to Mangalam Multiplex Pvt Ltd & Ors. sentences.text: 3. During the pendency of proceedings, the matter was settled amicably between the parties vide settlement deed dated 05.04.2021 executed between the petitioner No.1 company and complainants.

As per settlement, the petitioner No.1 company has paid the entire due amount against the loan to ICICI Bank and also paid Rs.1,52,25,654/- to complainants which includes the principal amount of Rs.93,70,932/- paid by them to petitioner No.1 company towards the purchase of Unit and compensation.
Pursuant to settlement, the complainants do not wish to pursue the complaint against any of the petitioners.

4. The complainant No.2, present for self and also on behalf of respondent No.3 - her daughter, has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners and the affidavits of both complainants are at pages No.47-50 of the paperbook.
The respondent No.2 states they have no claim against petitioners and they have no objection if the FIR is quashed as they have received the compensation from petitioner No.1 company.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainants have settled all the disputes and have received the settled amount as also compensation from petitioner No.1 company.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
6. Accordingly, both petitions are allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.72/2021 under Section 406/420/468/471/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Chitranjan Park and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
JANUARY 19, 2023
